`reliever_generic()` extends the search engine to an interval loss supplied in
R. The same function declares its outputs and evaluates fitted intervals.

## Minimum contract

Before searching, `reliever_generic()` makes a virtual call with
`is_virtual_run = TRUE`. Return either a positive integer or a list containing
`n_loss_outputs` and optional `loss_output_meta`.

During the search, the function fits observations `l:r`, scores observations
`l_end:r_end`, and returns `list(loss = ...)`. The loss must have one row per
scored observation and one column per declared output. A vector is accepted for
a single output.

## Worked example

This loss fits a multivariate mean and returns the mean squared residual for
each evaluation row.

```{r custom-loss}
library(relieverChangepoint)

custom_mean_loss <- function(data, l, r, l_end = l, r_end = r,
                             save_model = FALSE,
                             is_virtual_run = FALSE) {
  if (is_virtual_run) {
    return(list(
      n_loss_outputs = 1L,
      loss_output_meta = data.frame(
        loss_output_id = 1L,
        row_type = "custom_mean",
        loss_kind = "rss"
      )
    ))
  }

  data <- as.matrix(data)
  center <- colMeans(data[l:r, , drop = FALSE])
  residual <- sweep(
    data[l_end:r_end, , drop = FALSE],
    MARGIN = 2L,
    STATS = center
  )
  list(loss = rowMeans(residual^2))
}

set.seed(2026)
n_seg <- 100L
x <- rbind(
  matrix(rnorm(n_seg * 5, 0, 0.5), n_seg, 5),
  matrix(rnorm(n_seg * 5, 4, 0.5), n_seg, 5),
  matrix(rnorm(n_seg * 5, -4, 0.5), n_seg, 5)
)

path <- reliever_generic(
  data = x,
  reg_fun = custom_mean_loss,
  cpn_max = 4,
  dm = 15,
  cov_rate = 0.7,
  method = "SN",
  dc_grid_size = 10
)

selected <- select_by_run(result = path, cpn_crit = "rss_sic")
selected
stopifnot(identical(selected$K_hat, 2L))
```

## Metadata and multiple outputs

`loss_output_meta` may include `loss_output_id`, `row_type`, `hyper_value`,
`hyper_name`, `default_selection`, and `loss_kind`. Metadata drive readable
summaries, plotting defaults, and explicit output selection. Unrecognized
columns are retained.

When several outputs are declared, `run_cpd_ids` controls which output losses
receive changepoint searches. Advanced users should use explicit `run_ids` when
comparing only deliberately comparable stored paths.

## Outer-CV compatibility

Use `cv.reliever_generic()` when the interval model can be trained on one set
of rows and evaluated on held-out rows through the same loss contract. The
function selects a candidate and returns an automatic full-data refit in
`full_data_fit`.

For interval-level cross-fitting, start from `reg_fun_crossfit_template()`. A
classifier whose fit requires a global fold partition must use ordered
prediction folds; see `reg_fun_clf_crossfit_template()`.
